flashcard_sets.title: The USA and the five BRICS countries

flashcards.back: A country with great power and influence over other countries around the world. Its power comes from its economy, military, politics and culture.
When one country is the leading power in the world and has influence over most other countries.
A group of large emerging economies: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. More countries have joined the group since 2024.
A country with high incomes, good healthcare and education, and a high quality of life. For example, the UK and the USA.
A country whose economy is growing quickly as it builds more industry. For example, Brazil, India and China.
A country with lower incomes and a lower quality of life, which is still developing its economy and services.
Informal settlements (slums) in Brazilian cities, often built by people themselves on hillsides. Rocinha in Rio de Janeiro is one of the largest.
Not having enough money to meet basic needs such as food, clean water and a home.
Lacking things that most people have, such as good housing, healthcare, education or jobs.
A system where the state owns and controls land and businesses, and one party rules. The USSR was communist.
A system where people and private companies own businesses and try to make a profit. The USA is capitalist.
An explosion at the Chernobyl nuclear power station in Ukraine (then part of the USSR) in April 1986. It released radiation over a wide area.
The area around Chernobyl where people are not allowed to live because of radiation. It reaches about 30 kilometres from the power station.
When one country takes control of another place and rules it, often taking its resources. Britain ruled India until 1947.
Cities with more than 10 million people. For example, Mumbai and São Paulo.
A city that is much bigger and more important than any other city in its country. For example, London in the UK.
A company that operates in more than one country. It is often called a TNC. Foxconn is an example.
When a company or government from one country puts money into another country, for example by building a factory there.
Treating people unfairly to gain from their work, for example by paying very low wages or making them work very long hours.
A system in South Africa from 1948 to the early 1990s that kept people apart by race. Black South Africans had far fewer rights. It ended with free elections in 1994.

flashcards.front: USA: why is it a superpower?
flashcards.back: It has the largest economy in the world, the biggest military spending, and strong cultural influence through films, music and brands.
Capital: Brasília. Biggest city: São Paulo. Language: Portuguese. Most of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil.
Capital: Moscow. It is the largest country in the world by area. Biomes include tundra and taiga (cold forest).
Capital: New Delhi. Biggest city: Mumbai. Ruled by Britain until 1947. Famous attraction: the Taj Mahal in Agra.
Capital: Beijing. Biggest city: Shanghai. It has the second largest economy in the world. Famous attraction: the Great Wall.
It has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein. Biggest city: Johannesburg. Famous attractions: Table Mountain and Kruger National Park.
Cattle ranching, logging, mining and soya farming. Cutting down the forest is called deforestation.
A big city in Brazil, famous for Christ the Redeemer, Copacabana beach and the Rocinha favela.
Push factors make people leave a place, like no jobs in the village. Pull factors draw people to a place, like work in the city.

quiz.q: Which of these is a feature of a superpower?
quiz.explain: Superpowers have strong economies and militaries, and influence other countries.

quiz.q: After the USSR broke up in 1991, how many superpowers were left?
quiz.explain: The USA was left as the only superpower. This is called global hegemony.

quiz.q: What is the capital of the USA?
quiz.explain: Washington DC is the capital. New York is the largest city.

quiz.q: Which is an example of the USA's cultural influence around the world?
quiz.explain: Hollywood films, music and brands spread American culture around the world.

quiz.q: What was the Cold War?
options: A war fought in the Arctic
A war between Brazil and Russia
A long period of rivalry between the USA and the USSR
quiz.explain: The Cold War was a rivalry between the two superpowers from the late 1940s to 1991.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Brazil?
quiz.explain: Brasília is the capital. São Paulo is the biggest city.

quiz.q: Which is a major threat to the Amazon rainforest?
quiz.explain: Trees are cut down for cattle farming, soya, logging and mining.

quiz.q: Rocinha is a large favela in which city?
quiz.explain: Rocinha is in Rio de Janeiro. It is one of the largest favelas in Brazil.

quiz.q: What is the main language spoken in Brazil?
quiz.explain: Brazil was colonised by Portugal, so Portuguese is the main language.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Russia?
quiz.explain: Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia.

quiz.q: In which year did the USSR break up?
quiz.explain: The USSR broke up in 1991 into 15 separate countries, including Russia and Ukraine.

quiz.q: Which is one reason the USSR collapsed?
options: It had too many superpower allies
quiz.explain: The economy was struggling, the arms race was expensive, and many republics wanted independence.

quiz.q: What happened in Ukraine in February 2022?
options: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine
Ukraine became part of Russia by vote
quiz.explain: In February 2022 Russia invaded Ukraine. The war has caused many deaths and forced millions of people to leave their homes.

quiz.q: What was one consequence of the Chernobyl disaster in 1986?
options: A new city was built next to it
Nearby towns were evacuated and an exclusion zone was set up
Radiation stayed only inside the building
quiz.explain: The town of Pripyat was evacuated, and people still cannot live in the exclusion zone.

quiz.q: Which country ruled India until 1947?
quiz.explain: Britain ruled India until independence in 1947. This period is called the British Raj.

quiz.q: Dharavi is a large slum in which city?
quiz.explain: Dharavi is in Mumbai. It is one of the largest slums in Asia.

quiz.q: Which is a pull factor that brings people to Mumbai?
options: The chance of jobs in the city
quiz.explain: Pull factors attract people to a place. Push factors make people leave a place.

quiz.q: Where is the Taj Mahal?
quiz.explain: The Taj Mahal is in Agra. It is one of India's most famous tourist attractions.

quiz.q: What is the capital of China?
quiz.explain: Beijing is the capital. Shanghai is the largest city.

quiz.q: What is Foxconn?
options: A transnational company that makes electronics
quiz.explain: Foxconn makes electronics for brands such as Apple in large factories in China.

quiz.q: Why has Foxconn been criticised?
options: For harsh working conditions, such as very long hours
quiz.explain: Reports have described long hours, low pay and strict rules for workers. This is exploitation.

quiz.q: Why is China called a new world superpower?
options: Its economy has grown very fast
quiz.explain: China now has the second largest economy in the world.

quiz.q: When did apartheid begin in South Africa?
quiz.explain: Apartheid laws began in 1948. It ended with free elections in 1994.

quiz.q: Who became South Africa's first Black president in 1994?
quiz.explain: Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison and became president in 1994.

quiz.q: What was a consequence of apartheid?
options: Black South Africans had worse jobs, schools and housing
quiz.explain: Apartheid caused deep inequality, which still affects South Africa today.

quiz.q: Compared with most of Africa, South Africa's economy is:
options: One of the largest and most industrial
quiz.explain: South Africa is one of the most developed economies in Africa, but it has big gaps between rich and poor.

quiz.q: Which of these is an emerging country?
quiz.explain: Brazil's economy is growing fast as it builds more industry.

quiz.q: What is a megacity?
options: A city with more than 10 million people
A city with a big port
quiz.explain: Mumbai and São Paulo are megacities.

quiz.q: London is much bigger than any other UK city. What is London called?
quiz.explain: A primate city is much bigger and more important than any other city in its country.

learn.title: What is a superpower?
learn.text: A superpower is a country with power and influence all over the world. The power comes from four things: a big economy, a strong military, political influence and a culture that spreads abroad.

learn.title: The USA
learn.text: The USA has the largest economy in the world and spends the most on its military. Its films, music and brands are known everywhere. It leads alliances such as NATO.

learn.title: Hegemony
learn.text: From the late 1940s to 1991 the USA and the USSR were rivals in the Cold War. When the USSR broke up, the USA was the only superpower left. This is called global hegemony.

learn.title: Three types of country
learn.text: Developed countries, like the UK, have high incomes and good services. Emerging countries, like Brazil, India and China, are growing fast. Developing countries have lower incomes and fewer services.

learn.title: Poverty and deprivation
learn.text: Poverty means not having enough money for basic needs. Deprivation means missing things most people have, such as a good home, healthcare or school.

learn.title: Big cities
learn.text: A megacity has more than 10 million people, like Mumbai or São Paulo. A primate city is much bigger than any other city in its country, like London in the UK.

learn.title: Brazil
learn.text: Brazil is the largest country in South America. Its capital is Brasília and its biggest city is São Paulo. People speak Portuguese. Rio de Janeiro is famous for Christ the Redeemer and Copacabana beach.

learn.title: The Amazon
learn.text: Most of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil. It has more kinds of plants and animals than anywhere else, and many tribes live there. Cattle ranching, logging, mining and soya farming are destroying parts of it.

learn.title: Favelas
learn.text: Favelas are informal settlements in Brazilian cities. Rocinha in Rio is one of the largest. Many have poor services and problems with crime, but they also have strong communities.

learn.title: Russia
learn.text: Russia is the largest country in the world by area. Its capital is Moscow. Much of it is cold, with tundra in the far north and taiga, a huge conifer forest, further south.

learn.title: The end of the USSR
learn.text: Russia was the biggest part of the USSR, a communist country. The USSR broke up in 1991 because of economic problems, the cost of the arms race and republics wanting independence.

learn.title: Chernobyl
learn.text: In April 1986 a reactor at Chernobyl in Ukraine exploded during a badly run safety test. Radiation spread across Europe. The town of Pripyat was evacuated and an exclusion zone was set up.

learn.title: Ukraine, 2022
learn.text: Ukraine became independent when the USSR broke up. In February 2022 Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The war has caused many deaths and forced millions of people from their homes.

learn.title: India
learn.text: India's capital is New Delhi and its biggest city is Mumbai. It has the Himalayas in the north, the Thar Desert and tropical coasts. The Taj Mahal in Agra is its most famous sight.

learn.title: Colonial history
learn.text: Britain ruled India until 1947. This period is called the British Raj. India won independence in 1947 after a long campaign led by people such as Gandhi.

learn.title: Dharavi
learn.text: Dharavi in Mumbai is one of Asia's largest slums. Push factors drive people out of villages, such as a lack of work. Pull factors draw them to the city, such as jobs.

learn.title: Street scams
learn.text: Busy tourist areas in Mumbai and New Delhi have street scammers. Common tricks include fake guides, taxis that take the long way and people who say your hotel has closed.

learn.title: China
learn.text: China's capital is Beijing and its largest city is Shanghai. It has the Gobi Desert, the Himalayas and huge river plains. Tourists visit the Great Wall, the Forbidden City and the Terracotta Army.

learn.title: A new superpower
learn.text: China's economy has grown very fast since the 1980s. It now has the second largest economy in the world, and its factories make goods sold everywhere.

learn.title: Foxconn
learn.text: Foxconn is a transnational corporation that makes electronics, such as phones for Apple, in huge factories in China. It has been criticised for long hours, low pay and strict rules for workers.

learn.title: South Africa
learn.text: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein. Its largest city is Johannesburg. Tourists visit Table Mountain and Kruger National Park.

learn.title: Compared with the rest of Africa
learn.text: South Africa has one of the largest and most industrial economies in Africa. But the gap between rich and poor people there is one of the biggest in the world.

learn.title: Apartheid
learn.text: From 1948, laws kept people apart by race. Black South Africans had worse schools, jobs and homes, and could not vote. Apartheid ended with free elections in 1994, when Nelson Mandela became president.
